text:
I didn't write `notes/tighter-zoom.json` and didn't change anything in the app. The type declarations don't say what `camera.radius` reads after each case, so any numbers I wrote would be guesses.

What the declarations show:
- `radius` and `center` are plain fields on `GeospatialCamera`, and `limits.radiusMax` is a plain field on `GeospatialLimits`. Nothing in the types says that assigning `radius` or `center` clamps anything.
- `setGeospatialOrientation` and the `_setOrientation` field suggest that orientation changes go through a path that may apply limits, but the types don't say whether it does.
- Unlike `ArcRotateCamera`, the geospatial camera has no `_clampToLimits` in its declarations, so there is no visible clamp hook to rely on.

To settle the four values, you need the library's implementation of the geospatial camera's `radius` and `center` setters and of `setGeospatialOrientation`, or a run of the four cases against the real 1.39.0 build.

If you only need the zoom to respect the new limit, you don't have to depend on any of that. Clamp it explicitly right after changing the limit:

```ts
camera.limits.radiusMax = 2000;
camera.radius = Math.min(camera.radius, camera.limits.radiusMax);
```
